en.name: Farro, whole grain
en.summary: Farro is an ancient hulled wheat — emmer, and sometimes einkorn or spelt — sold whole with its bran and germ. Kept airtight and out of the light it runs about 6 months in the cupboard, and 12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: Farro benefits from being stored in airtight containers and out of direct light, and on those terms it keeps about 6 months. As with any whole grain, the limit is the germ: it carries oil, and oil turns. Semi-pearled and pearled farro, which has had some or all of the bran abraded off, keeps rather better than the truly whole grain but loses the fibre that made you buy it. Keep the jar in the coolest, darkest cupboard you have, and not above the hob.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for farro, so this page gives none. An airtight jar in the fridge is still a sensible home for an opened bag in a hot, humid kitchen, since cold slows the germ oil from turning — but the container must seal properly, grain takes up smells, and a cold jar opened in a warm kitchen collects condensation on whatever is inside it. Let it warm up before you open it.
en.freezer: The freezer doubles it, to 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), in an airtight container or a heavy freezer bag with the air pressed out. This is the right answer for a big bag, and it settles any question about weevil eggs brought home from a bulk bin. Cook farro straight from frozen — no thawing needed, and the extra cooking time is negligible. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality.
spoilage: A bitter or paint-like smell from rancid germ oil.
A musty, damp smell or grains clumping together.
Webbing, small moths or fine dust in the jar.
Grains that stay chalky in the middle however long they simmer.
tips: Decant bags into airtight jars the day you buy them and date the lid.
Freeze large bags immediately rather than after they have sat in the cupboard.
Smell before cooking; rancidity is not visible.
Buy semi-pearled if you cook it rarely — it keeps better and cooks faster.

faq.a: About 6 months airtight in a cool, dark cupboard, or 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 12 months at −18 °C in an airtight container, and you can cook it straight from frozen.

faq.q: Why does whole farro keep less time than white rice?
faq.a: Because it still has its bran and germ, and the oil in the germ goes rancid. Polished white rice has had both removed.

zh.name: 法羅麥（全粒）
zh.summary: Farro 是一種古代帶殼小麥（多為二粒小麥，有時是單粒小麥或斯佩爾特），以保留麩皮與胚芽的全粒形式販售。密封避光保存，櫥櫃約 6 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 12 個月。
zh.pantry: Farro 適合裝在密封容器裡、避免直射光，這樣大約可放 6 個月。和所有全穀一樣，限制它的是胚芽：胚芽含油，而油會變質。半拋光或全拋光的 farro 磨掉了部分或全部麩皮，比真正的全粒耐放一些，但也失去了你當初買它的那份纖維。罐子請放在家裡最涼、最暗的櫥櫃，不要放在爐台上方。
zh.fridge: Farro 沒有公布的冷藏期限，本頁也不給。不過在濕熱的廚房裡，開封後裝密封罐放冰箱仍然合理，因為低溫能延緩胚芽油脂變質——但容器必須真的密封，穀物會吸味道，而冰冷的罐子在溫暖廚房打開，裡面的東西就會結露。開封前先讓它回溫。
zh.freezer: 冷凍讓期限加倍，−18 °C 下 12 個月，裝密封容器或厚冷凍袋壓出空氣。大包裝就該這樣處理，也能一併解決散裝買回來的蟲卵問題。要煮時直接從冷凍下鍋——不必解凍，多出來的烹煮時間可以忽略。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。
spoilage: 聞到胚芽油走油耗後的苦味或油漆味。
有潮霉味，或麥粒結成塊。
罐內出現絲網、小蛾或細粉屑。
不管煮多久，中心還是硬硬粉粉的。
tips: 買回來當天就倒進密封罐，並在蓋子上寫日期。
大包裝要馬上冷凍，不要先在櫥櫃放一陣子。
煮之前先聞；油耗是看不出來的。
很少煮的話買半拋光版本——比較耐放也比較快熟。

faq.a: 密封、陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 12 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下密封容器 12 個月，而且能直接從冷凍下鍋煮。

faq.q: 為什麼全粒 farro 比白米不耐放？
faq.a: 因為它還帶著麩皮和胚芽，而胚芽裡的油會走油耗。精白米兩者都已經磨掉了。
